HG33-buteyko-e.was_md: Then work on your reduced breathing / Buteyko’ breathing. (NOTE: there are some good things to be said for slowing your breathing down, if you are breathing too much, or panicked. However, please don’t hold your breath until you are air hungry, which can make you more anxious in the short term. Go slow on this.) Inhale small amounts through your nose, exhale quietly through it, and pause only if comfortable. Can you make your breathing very quiet? If you feel bad, dizzy, or panicky, or have medical issues, STOP!
HG33-buteyko-e.new_md: Then work on your reduced breathing / Buteyko’ breathing. Breathe in small amounts through your nose and let it out quietly, through your nose too. Only pause if that's comfortable. Can you make your breathing very quiet? If you feel bad, dizzy, or panicky, or have medical issues, STOP!

HG35-forgive-e2.was_md: We can not ‘force’ forgiveness on ourselves, it has to come from a place of understanding otherwise it can be bypassing. However, if we remain in the anger forever, we are allowing the injury to dictate how we live our lives in the present. So how do we hold all of this? We simply remember that it can all be true: the harm happened, the boundary still matters, the person is still accountable, and forgiveness may come later on its own.
